caption_en:
One of these walks wins on length. The view is your call. 🌊

The Tel Aviv promenade runs about 14 km from Jaffa to the north, past 13 beaches (Tel Aviv-Yafo Municipality), in a city of about half a million people (Israel CBS). How it ranks against famous seafronts, by length:

🇪🇬 Alexandria Corniche: over 16 km (over ten miles, Wikipedia)
🇮🇱 Tel Aviv: 14 km (8.7 miles, Tel Aviv-Yafo Municipality)
🇶🇦 Doha Corniche: 7 km (Visit Qatar)
🇫🇷 Promenade des Anglais, Nice: almost 7 km (Explore Nice Côte d'Azur)
🇦🇺 Bondi to Coogee walk: 6 km (Destination NSW)
🇱🇧 Beirut Corniche: 4.8 km (Wikipedia)
🇧🇷 Copacabana: 4 km (National Endowment for the Humanities)
🇺🇸 Venice Beach boardwalk: about 3.2 km (Wikipedia)

Beach visits a year: Venice Beach about 10 million (ABC News, 2023), Tel Aviv 8.5 million bathers (Tel Aviv-Yafo Municipality). The others publish no official count, so we show no data.

Beauty has no fair ranking. You decide: which one would you walk? Tell me in the comments.

Photos (Wikimedia Commons): Yong Woo Park (CC BY 4.0); Daniel Mayer (CC BY-SA 4.0); Txllxt TxllxT (CC BY-SA 4.0); Wilfredor (CC0); Wusel007 (CC BY-SA 3.0); Dr. Avishai Teicher, PikiWiki Israel (CC BY 2.5). AI voice.
caption_he:
הטיילת של תל אביב: כ־14 ק"מ מיפו צפונה, 13 חופים ו־8.5 מיליון רוחצים בשנה (עיריית תל אביב־יפו).
באורך היא במקום השני בעולם מבין הטיילות המפורסמות, אחרי הקורניש של אלכסנדריה (יותר מ־16 ק"מ). דוחה וניס כ־7, בונדי לקוג'י 6, ביירות 4.8, קופקבנה 4, ונציה ביץ' כ־3.2.
ויופי? את זה אין מדד הוגן שמודד. אתם מחליטים: באיזו טיילת הייתם הולכים?

lines.line: Fourteen kilometres of seafront. The best on Earth?
Tel Aviv's promenade runs from Jaffa all the way north. Thirteen beaches on one walk.
So let's race it against the world's famous seafronts. By length.
Alexandria's Corniche: over sixteen kilometres. The Mediterranean champion.
Then Tel Aviv, fourteen. Doha and Nice, about seven each.
Bondi to Coogee, six. Beirut, almost five. Copacabana, four. Venice Beach, three.
Tel Aviv takes silver. Not bad for a city of half a million.
Now, how busy? Tel Aviv counts eight and a half million beach visits a year.
Venice Beach says about ten million. The others publish no official count.
And beauty? No ranking can measure that. So you decide.
Or Tel Aviv, beach after beach?
If you love Israeli facts, follow Noam Roz for more.
